'''Data goggles''' were specialized communications devices produced by the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] and commonly used aboard the [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and [[Transport/Legends|transports]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].

Data goggles were, to exterior appearances, simple eye-goggles that provided the wearer with real-time [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] displays within the eyecups. However, these goggles also included a cybernetic implant that provided the user with direct access to the starship's [[Central Control Computer/Legends|Central Control Computer]]. This meant [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] could literally activate shipboard systems with a thought. These goggles also included a disk-shaped [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] that fit over the wearer's mouth.

Notable wearers of data goggles include the navigator of the ''[[Revenue]]'', as well as [[Tey How/Legends|Tey How]] and [[Sil Unch]], who respectively served aboard the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']] and the [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']] used at the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]. Since the Neimoidian designers jealously guarded the schematics, data goggles were rarely used among non-Neimoidians.

==Behind the scenes==
Data goggles first appeared in [[1999]] with the release of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] and its tie-ins. In the reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'', the data goggles were referred to as "datagoggles."
